summary.intent: Evaluate the wisp-plugins prompts/agents against current Anthropic guidance on review slop, then investigate still-failing code reviews on Callisto changes (40, 42, 43, 44, 46) and fold the findings into the evaluation doc.
summary.outcome: Committed Part 3 of the evaluation doc (0f508236, signed, not pushed) with six revised suggestions, then pulled and read diffs and findings for Callisto changes 40/42/43/44/46 and added a trail 198 update to the evaluation README, with checks run and committed. The user was left to decide between running the first batch or measuring the reasoning-field and cache questions first.

repo: Evaluation doc lives at docs/evaluations/review-slop-learnings/README.md in the worktree .claude/worktrees/review-slop-evaluation of wisp-plugins; `just check` gates commits.

Plugins are largely free of dated prompt patterns (no 'think step by step', CRITICAL caps, retired model names); emphasis is light (31 NEVER, 4 MUST, 0 ALWAYS in ~23k words). The issue is structure and volume.
30 skills exist (not 33); descriptions are within the 1,536-char cap.
44 agents instruct a `reasoning` scratchpad, 30 show it in output examples, 12 schemas require it, and nothing consumes it.
The byte-identical constitution block (ADR 006) is justified by cross-agent cache sharing, but it is ~323 tokens, below the 512-token cacheable minimum, so the rationale looks unsupported.
Plugin hook scripts are unwired and only inject one language's hazards; the recommendation is to delete them and fix docs.
mason:evaluate and manifest scripts may overlap first-party `claude plugin validate`, `claude plugin eval` and `/skill-doctor`.
Entire has not ingested the hold-note session because its checkpoint is unpushed, so the local transcript must be read instead.
workflow: When Entire lacks a session, fall back to the local transcript for the same session.
Verify suspect facts from diffs (e.g., whether RETRY_RESET is real, tokenizer behavior on chunk-e409.js) before characterizing review findings.
Prefer Anthropic's tested prompt snippets over invented wording; A/B overly prescriptive prompts before rewriting.
Tier changes save little since Opus is 2x Sonnet; better levers are fewer calls, Haiku for mechanical work, and Opus instead of Fable for arch-auditor check mode.
Use fresh-context verifiers (independent gates) rather than self-critique.
